name: The Tanyosho Pine of Kubota Garden

location.address: Historic Core Garden, near the Heart Bridge, Kubota Garden, 9817 55th Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118

access: Free; Kubota Garden is a public city park, open daily, no entry fee
transport: Rainier Beach neighbourhood, south Seattle; nearest Metro bus stops on Renton Ave S, roughly 10 minute walk
verify_notes: Only one source found, so flagged per Step 2 (single-source rule) rather than dropped. Source is the City of Seattle's own official Kubota Garden Tree Walk PDF (Trees for Seattle programme, stop 8 of 14, chosen by Kubota Garden Foundation volunteers), fetched and read directly (not a search summary). Directly quoted: 'Located in the Historic Core Garden near the Heart Bridge. Early aerial photos of the garden show that Fujitaro Kubota planted 15-20 of them around the "drive" creating a light filtering tunnel of sorts. Today, after many winter storms and changing climate, only one of the original 90-year-old trees is left. A handful of "replacements" have been planted over the past 20 years.' Kubota Garden itself is well documented (Wikipedia, TCLF, Seattle Times): a public park since 1987, a City Historical Landmark since 1981, founded 1927 by Japanese immigrant gardener Fujitaro Kubota. This is a genuine single collectible point: the sole survivor of an original avenue, not the avenue itself (the brief's own distinction). Age of 'about 90 years' is the PDF's own figure (2019-published document; tree would now be closer to 95-100, kept as a broad range rather than sharpened). Location is the Historic Core Garden area of Kubota Garden; coordinate given is the garden's own centroid (approximate), not a mapped GPS point for this specific pine.

access: Free; Kubota Garden is a public city park, open daily, no entry fee

verify_notes: Only one source found (same official Kubota Garden Tree Walk PDF, stop 14), so flagged rather than dropped, same as sea_007. Directly quoted: 'Located in the Japanese Garden, it was garden founder Fujitaro Kubota's favorite tree. The white line on each leaf exudes brightness and light. The tree, carefully pruned for over 80 years, has beautiful limbs and lines.' No exact planting date given, only the pruning duration, so age is a broad floor (80+) rather than a tight estimate; if the garden dates to 1927 the tree cannot be older than the garden itself (99 years as of 2026), used as the age_max ceiling. A WebSearch AI summary conflated this tree's 'favorite tree' story with the Tanyosho pine's planting history; that conflation was caught by reading the PDF directly and is NOT reflected in either record here. Same park, same free public access as sea_007.
